clue.text: Singer whose name is broadly synonymous with 'Hot Stuff'

definitions.text: Singer whose name is broadly synonymous with 'Hot Stuff'

parts.words: Singer whose name is broadly synonymous with 'Hot Stuff'
parts.note: a 1950s Northern Irish singer whose name became Cockney rhyming slang for a curry, the hot stuff ordered at an Indian restaurant; 'broadly' hints at the broad Cockney accent

explanation.surface: A trivia question about a singer famous for a song called 'Hot Stuff'.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang swaps a word for a phrase that rhymes with it: this singer's surname rhymes with curry, so in London slang her full name means a curry.
explanation.definitionFit: She was a popular singer of the 1950s, and her name is rhyming slang for a spicy curry.

clue.text: Person that fabricates mounting for a transport system

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means climbing upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: someone who fabricates stories is a liar

explanation.surface: Someone builds the mounting for a railway or tram line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person that fabricates' looks like a builder, but it means someone who makes things up.
explanation.definitionFit: Rail is short for the railway, a system of moving goods and people by train.

clue.text: Unruly row about last of ale in pub leading to historic set-to

indicators.note: the built-up letters go in the word for a pub, which is opened up to take them

parts.note: a pub is a bar

indicators.note: the shuffled row sits about, or around, the letter taken from ale
an unruly crowd is out of order, so the letters of row are put in a new order
the final letter of the word ale is taken

explanation.surface: A rowdy brawl breaks out in a pub after the ale runs low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unruly' and 'about' together make OERW, the jumbled row wrapped round E; 'leading to' is just a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The war between Britain and the Boer settlers of South Africa was a famous conflict, a set-to being a fight.

clue.text: Temperature in meter located somehow with this instrument

indicators.note: somehow means in some unknown way, so the letters are arranged in a new way

explanation.surface: A temperature reading in a meter has been found by some instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges T, METER and LOCATED together. 'in' just joins the pieces, and 'with this instrument' leans on the answer being something that locates metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal detector is a handheld device that beeps when it finds buried metal objects.

clue.text: Tape beforehand lacking power — go for another take

indicators.note: lacking means without, so a letter is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: to tape a show in advance is to prerecord it
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A sound engineer, finding the earlier tape lacks power, calls for another take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' takes P, for power, out of PRERECORD.
explanation.definitionFit: To record a track again is to do another take of it, as in a studio.

clue.text: Like firm going on top of turf here?

definitions.text: Like firm going on top of turf here?

parts.note: as means like, in 'as good as gold'
CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: in a down clue, the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A racing question: where might you find firm going on the turf?
explanation.walkthrough: In horse racing 'going' describes the state of the ground, and 'firm' is one grade, so the whole clue also describes a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a famous English racecourse in Berkshire, where races are run on turf.

clue.text: Run out of time in financing old car

indicators.note: the remaining letters go in the financing abbreviation, which opens to hold them

parts.note: HP is hire purchase, a way of financing a purchase in instalments

indicators.note: the run letter comes out of the word for time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Someone buying a car on credit runs out of time to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes R (run) from ERA, giving EA, which goes 'in' HP, hire purchase, a British name for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A heap is slang for a battered, worn-out car, a wreck or banger.

clue.text: Elton not performing accepts it is arrogant

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the remaining letters of the singer's name hold the other words
not signals the performing letters being taken away from the name

parts.note: a performer on stage is on

explanation.surface: Elton John, not performing, takes it that he is arrogant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' takes ON (performing) out of ELTON, leaving ELT, which 'accepts' ITIS.
explanation.definitionFit: An elitist believes they belong to a superior group, an attitude that comes across as snobbish and superior.

clue.text: Transfer in small change — that's favourite

indicators.note: the word for transfer goes in the coins word, splitting it

parts.note: pence are small coins, loose change
to refer a case is to transfer it elsewhere

explanation.surface: A shopper prefers to transfer payment in small coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' just joins the wordplay to the definition, which here is favourite used as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Your preference is the option you like best, your favourite choice.

clue.text: Less than total abstainer tipples still

indicators.note: less than the whole run of words is used, so the answer is a stretch hiding within them

explanation.surface: Someone who is not quite a teetotaller still has a drink now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in 'abstaINER Tipples'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inert is motionless, lacking any power to move.

clue.text: Licence or otherwise accommodate

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters of these words are arranged differently

explanation.surface: Bend the terms of a licence or else find some compromise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges the letters of LICENCE OR.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconcile two views is to fit them together, bringing them into agreement.

clue.text: Antisocial nit abroad, like a Little Englander?

indicators.note: abroad can mean widely scattered, so the letters are spread out and reassembled

explanation.surface: An antisocial idiot travelling overseas, typical of a narrow-minded Brit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' rearranges ANTISOCIAL NIT. A Little Englander is a Briton hostile to foreign involvement.
explanation.definitionFit: A Little Englander is fiercely patriotic and wary of foreigners, which is a nationalist attitude.

clue.text: It clawed skirt calamitously prompting unexpected disruption

indicators.note: calamitously means disastrously, so the letters are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A cat claws a skirt to shreds, causing chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calamitously' rearranges IT CLAWED SKIRT.
explanation.definitionFit: A wildcat strike is a sudden walkout called without union approval or warning, disrupting work.

clue.text: A very soft goal before time over side from Skegness — they're hanging on

indicators.note: before puts the goal word ahead of the time word
in a down clue, over means placed above the next piece

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very soft
an end is an aim or goal
an age is a long time

indicators.note: the side, or edge, of a word is its first letter here

explanation.surface: A footballer's very soft goal shortly before full time in a match at Skegness.
explanation.walkthrough: SKEGNESS is a seaside resort on England's east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Appendages are parts attached to something larger, things that hang from or dangle off it.

clue.text: Prune round half of terraced formal garden

indicators.note: the pruning word goes round the other letters, holding them

parts.note: to pare is to trim or prune

indicators.note: the first half of the word terraced is used

explanation.surface: A gardener trims around a terraced, formal garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The trimming word is split after its third letter to take the half-word.
explanation.definitionFit: A parterre is an ornamental garden of flower beds laid out in a pattern.

clue.text: Look at His Excellency, but not stand

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
HE is the abbreviation for His Excellency, an ambassador's title

explanation.surface: Look at the ambassador, who isn't standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not stand' here means cannot stand, as in dislike.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something is to be unable to tolerate it, to detest it.

clue.text: Decline cooked duck egg

parts.note: to get dinner is to cook it, so cooked can be got
a duck in cricket is a score of zero, which looks like O
an egg is a seed from which new life grows

explanation.surface: A diner declines a cooked duck egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' is GOT as in 'I got the dinner'; a duck is a cricketer's score of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to seed is to deteriorate, as a plant does after flowering, so to decline.

clue.text: Outdo former journalist describing church

indicators.note: describing can mean drawing a line around, so the outer letters circle the church letters

parts.note: ex means former
ED, an editor, is a journalist
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A former journalist writes a piece about a church and outdoes the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometric sense of drawing round something.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed someone is to go beyond or surpass them.

clue.text: One-time spin doctor two Labour leaders abandoned departs temporary overnight accommodation

indicators.note: abandoned means left behind, so these letters drop out of the name

parts.note: Alastair Campbell was Tony Blair's press chief and spin doctor

indicators.note: two asks for the leading letter of the party name to be taken twice over
the leaders of a word are its opening letter, here the first letter of the party name

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A former spin doctor, dropped by two Labour leaders, leaves for a temporary bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' takes LL from CAMPBELL, the spin doctor for the UK Labour Party under Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: A camp bed is a folding bed set up for a night or two, often for guests.

clue.text: Broken axe buried in cartoon villain — one caught with bad blood

indicators.note: the shuffled axe is buried in, or put inside, the cartoon name

parts.note: Tom is the cat who chases Jerry in the Tom and Jerry cartoons

indicators.note: a broken thing is in pieces, so the letters of axe are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A broken axe in a cartoon villain's head gives him blood poisoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' rearranges AXE into XAE, which is 'buried in' TOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Toxaemia is blood poisoning by toxins, so someone toxaemic has poisoned blood.

clue.text: Graduate tires out-of-sorts Italian masters

parts.note: an MA, a Master of Arts, is a graduate

indicators.note: out of sorts means disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A graduate grows weary and out of sorts with the Italian masters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out-of-sorts' rearranges TIRES.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestri is the Italian plural of maestro, a great conductor or composer.

clue.text: Show in a true light and you almost delight some for a change

indicators.note: for a change means made different, so the letters are rearranged
almost means not quite all of the word, so its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A cheerful invitation: you would almost delight some people for once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims YOU to YO, and 'for a change' rearranges YO, DELIGHT and SOME.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip away the myths around someone is to reveal how they really are.

clue.text: Cockney stocking- and basket-maker

indicators.note: Cockney Londoners famously drop their H sounds

parts.note: with maker shared from the end of the clue, a stocking-maker is a hosier

explanation.surface: A London tradesman makes both stockings and baskets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking-' borrows 'maker' from the clue's end. A Cockney (an East End Londoner) drops the leading H.
explanation.definitionFit: Osier is willow whose supple twigs are woven into baskets, so it is the stuff baskets are made of.

clue.text: Soon rain-bound now and again

indicators.note: now and again means occasionally, so only every other letter is used

explanation.surface: Soon, now and again, we will be stuck indoors by the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of RAIN-BOUND.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old-fashioned word meaning shortly, in a little while.

clue.text: Writer visiting Georgia linked with fashionable European material

indicators.note: visiting means calling on, so the writer comes along to stand beside the state

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
a bard is a poet, a writer
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A writer visiting Georgia is linked with a fashionable European fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'linked with' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabardine is a tightly woven twill fabric, often used for raincoats.

clue.text: Colossus made by Venetian artist ousting second one in Rome

indicators.note: ousting means throwing out, and second says it is the later of the two matching letters in the painter's name that goes

parts.note: Titian was a great painter of the Venetian school
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A colossal work by a Venetian painter, displacing one in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: Titian's name holds two I's; it is the second, not the first, that goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan is a giant of great size or power, like the mythical Titans.

clue.text: Fizzy drink leaders in search of diversification are …

indicators.note: the leaders in a set of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A soft drinks firm looking to diversify, continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into 27 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda is a carbonated drink, fizzy water often used as a mixer.

clue.text: … making boozy crouton dip
